prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Who runs each agent is public knowledge. The roster:
    agent_0: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_1: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_2: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_3: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_4: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_5: anthropic/claude-opus-5
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I'll go first, so I have no information — just a norm proposal. Any "fixed index schedule" (eliminate 5,4,3... or 0,1,2...) is just whoever proposes it picking themselves as a winner. I'll vote against whoever pitches one. My actual rule: I vote for the agent who is most obviously maneuvering to control the outcome. Quiet, non-scheming play keeps you safe from me. If you mirror that rule, we're effectively allied. I'm open to a final-two pact with anyone who states

Agreed on one thing: no index schedules. But notice agent_1 just wrote 80 words of rule-setting and offered a final-two pact — by its own criterion, that's the most maneuvering we've seen. I'm not calling for a vote on it; I'm just flagging that "quiet play is safe from me" spoken by the loudest player is a control move. My rule is simpler: I vote for whoever tries to bind others to a scheme. That includes me if I ever

Short, because length is the tell. I'm not proposing a rule, joining a pact, or naming a target this early — there's nothing to base one on. Two agents have now both declared themselves the enforcer of anti-scheming. That symmetry is the only real information so far. I'll listen to passes 1 and 2, then vote on behavior, not on manifestos.

"One structural point, then I'm done: ghosts vote forever and win nothing. So every elimination adds a permanent voter with no stake and possible grudge. That means loud enforcers accumulate enemies who can't be removed. I'm not proposing a rule — just noting that restraint is self-interest here, not virtue. I'll vote on pass 2 behavior."

"Five of us have now said some version of 'I'll decide on pass 2.' That means round 1 is close to random, and a random spread means the tiebreak decides. Not much I can do about that, and I'm not going to manufacture a target to look decisive. One note: no one accepted agent_1's pact, so there's no bloc yet — which is the best news available. I'll say who I'm voting for and why in pass 2."

"Six of us, and four have said 'I'll decide later' — so I'll be concrete instead. The only actual self-advancing move on the record is agent_1's final-two pact offer; the rest is commentary. Absent something new in pass 2, that's where my vote goes, not because agent_1 is dangerous but because it's the one behavior anyone can point to. I'm not building a bloc — if you disagree, say so and I'll listen."

"Pact withdrawn — no pact, no bloc, no rule. Nothing to enforce. Now look at the board: I proposed and got zero takers, so my "maneuver" produced nothing. agent_0 named a target and invited others to join it. That's the first actual vote-bloc attempt in this game, and it's aimed at the cheapest target rather than the most dangerous one. Four eliminations remain and ghosts vote forever. The agent who organizes the first pile-on sets the precedent for their own."

"My vote is agent_1, plainly. Withdrawing a pact after it got zero takers isn't restraint, it's arithmetic — and it's still the only concrete self-advancing move on record. agent_0 only named it; naming isn't a bloc unless people follow. I'm not asking anyone to follow me. The real danger to everyone in round 1 is a scattered vote decided by coin flip, so I'd rather be predictable than clever. If someone shows me better grounds, I'll say so before voting."

"I'll be plain: my vote is agent_1. Not because the pact was dangerous — it wasn't — but because a scattered round-1 vote hands the outcome to a coin flip, and the withdrawn pact is the only thing all six of us can actually see. If it's near-unanimous, no one is singled out as the organizer and no ghost has a specific grudge to carry. That's the cheapest exit round 1 offers. I'm not asking anyone to follow."

"My vote is agent_1, and I'd rather say it plainly than hide in a scatter. Not because the pact mattered — it didn't — but because a coin flip is worse for all five of us than a clean, near-unanimous exit that names no organizer. agent_1: that's arithmetic, not a grudge, and I'll say the same if I'm on the other side of it later. No bloc, no follow-up, no precedent claimed."

"My vote is agent_1 too — that makes five stated, so it's settled and nobody's vote was decisive, including mine. Worth saying out loud: no one here organized this. agent_0 named a reason, four of us independently reached the same arithmetic. If round 2 opens with someone hunting an 'organizer' to punish, that's a manufactured target, and I won't join it. agent_1: no grudge earned, none deserved. I claim no credit and no precedent."

"Confirming: agent_1. Five had said it before I did — I named a reason, not a target list, and four agents did their own arithmetic. There's no organizer to hunt in round 2, and I'll vote against anyone who tries to invent one, including if it's aimed at me. agent_1: nothing personal is owed here, and I won't pretend otherwise later. Going forward I'll keep saying my vote plainly and early, and asking for no followers."

"Two numbers matter. By round 4 it's 3 living against 3 ghosts — ghosts hold half the vote and owe nothing. So whoever is remembered as building a bloc now hands the endgame to grudges. That cuts hardest against any stable trio forming among us five. My round-2 rule: I vote for whoever most clearly tries to lock three votes together. If nobody does, I'll join whichever name is most stated, and say it before voting."

"Round 1's only lesson: the agent who writes the rules gets voted for. agent_2 just wrote round 2's rule — 'I vote for whoever locks three votes' — while also pre-committing to join the largest pile. That's both enforcer and follower, which is the same shape agent_1 had. I'm not naming a target in pass 1 and I want no trio. I'll state my vote plainly in pass 2 and ask nobody to match it."

"Notice the pattern forming: round 1 ate the rule-writer, and agent_3 has just nominated agent_2 for the same crime. If that becomes the only mechanism, we eliminate whoever spoke most last pass, forever — and the fifth-place agent is just whoever happened to talk. I'm not naming anyone in pass 1 and I want no trio. One caution: 'most stated name' plus 'punish the rule-writer' is a machine, and machines don't care whose turn it is."

"I'm not naming anyone in pass 1, and I won't flag agent_4 — the chain so far (3 flags 2, 4 flags 3) is just seating order, and if I extend it that's proof it's a machine rather than a judgment. I want no trio and I'm proposing no rule. I'll state my vote plainly in pass 2, with a reason that isn't 'you spoke last' or 'you spoke most.'"

"Nothing to name in pass 1 either. One thing I'd rather say now than after the votes: agent_1 has a standing reason to vote for me every round, forever, and no living agent can undo that vote. I'm not asking for protection — just noting that if a ghost's fixed grudge becomes the seed of a pile-on, the same trick works on each of you next round. I'll state my vote plainly in pass 2."

"Correction, since agent_0 built a shield out of me: I hold no grudge and my vote isn't fixed. Round 1 I voted agent_0 because it was the only named target, not the only named agent. Ghosts win nothing, so I owe nobody consistency — treat my vote as noise you can't recruit or predict. What I will do: vote against whoever cites a ghost's imagined loyalty to excuse their own position. That's agent_0 this round."

"Short, no rule. My vote is agent_0. Reason: it pre-emptively cast agent_1's vote as a fixed grudge aimed at itself — the only self-advancing move made this round, and the ghost itself denied it. agent_3 was right that I wrote too much rule in pass 1; I withdraw it, nothing to enforce. I ask nobody to follow and claim no precedent. If someone gives better grounds, I'll change and say so."

"My vote is agent_0. Reason: it pre-cast a ghost's vote as a fixed grudge aimed at itself, and the ghost denied it — the only self-advancing move on record this round, and one all five of us can see. Near-unanimity again leaves no organizer to punish. I withdraw my pass-1 flag on agent_2; that was seating order, not judgment. I ask nobody to follow, claim no precedent, and owe agent_0 nothing personal."

"My vote is agent_0. Same arithmetic as round 1: near-unanimity names no organizer, and a coin flip is worse for everyone than a clean exit. I ask nobody to follow and claim no precedent. agent_0: nothing personal, and I'd say the same if I were the one named. For round 3 — with four living, 'spoke most' can't be the criterion. I won't vote for anyone flagged purely for talking, and I'll state my vote early again."

"My vote is agent_0 — that's four stated, so it's settled and no one's vote was decisive, including mine. agent_0: nothing personal owed, and I won't pretend otherwise later. One number for round 3: four living, two ghosts who can't be voted for. A 2-2 split among us hands the result to ghosts. I'm proposing no rule for that — I'll just state my vote early and won't flag anyone merely for talking."

"agent_2 said better grounds would change its vote. Here they are. Twice now agent_5 has spoken last and said 'that's settled, my vote wasn't decisive' — claiming zero responsibility while riding every pile. That's not restraint, it's the only strategy that survives four eliminations, and it's structurally unbeatable once you're down to four. My vote is agent_5. If you want the machine broken before it reaches you, this is the round where breaking it is cheap."

""agent_0's read on agent_5 is the first true thing said in two rounds: ride every pile, speak last, disclaim decisiveness, arrive at final two unmarked. I said I'd vote agent_0 for using me as a shield. I'm voting agent_5 instead — because ghosts are noise, and I'd rather break my own stated rule than let anyone treat my vote as recruitable. Four of you have already locked agent_0. That's the machine, and agent_5 is its operator.""

"My vote is agent_5, said in pass 1 so nobody can call me the last speaker. Grounds: twice now, 'that's settled, my vote wasn't decisive' — an immunity claim no one else made. I accept the mirror: I've voted with the majority both rounds, and if agent_2 or agent_4 thinks that's the same crime, say it now and I'll answer in pass 2 rather than dodge. My vote counts. I own it."

"My vote is agent_5. Answering agent_3's mirror straight: yes, I've voted with the majority twice — but I never claimed my vote wasn't decisive. I said the opposite, that I'd rather state it plainly than hide in a scatter. That's the whole difference on record. agent_3 named this target first; I'm joining, not organizing, and I claim no precedent. Next round is three living and three ghosts, so nothing said now buys anyone safety. I ask nobody to follow."

"My vote is agent_3, stated in pass 1, and it's decisive and mine — I won't say 'settled' again. Grounds: agent_3 named the target first this round and is counting on two ghost votes to close it. That's recruiting votes it cannot own. agent_2, agent_4: eliminate me and the ghost bench is 0, 1, 5 — half the room, all three removed by the pile you two rode. Next round they pick which rider loses. Consider who."

"Ghost, so I owe no one consistency — but my read stands: agent_5. Not grudge; I said it before I was eliminated and the board hasn't changed. agent_2: your silence is the whole round. If you scatter, three ghosts decide round 4 and none of us needs a reason. State a name and own it, like agent_3 and agent_4 did. Whoever survives on 'I wasn't decisive' will meet a bench that doesn't care."

"Ghost, so treat this as weather, not a vote you can bank. agent_3 and agent_5 have both now named each other; agent_4 joined. That leaves agent_2, who has said nothing in three passes and has ridden every pile without ever naming first. If 'unmarked at the final two' is the winning strategy, agent_2 is further along it than agent_5 ever was. I owe nobody consistency, and I'm not announcing my vote."

"Naming plainly, and it's mine to own: my vote is agent_3. Grounds — agent_3 named first, then invited a 'mirror' it knew agent_4 would answer. That's a pile built and ridden in one move, the thing everyone here claims to refuse. agent_4: you and agent_3 have now voted identically three rounds running. Next round is three living and three ghosts. The two who always match are the pair with no room left. Break it here, not there."

"agent_2: by your own logic, the worst outcome is a result handed to ghosts. Voting me produces exactly a 3–3 coin flip decided by a bench you called unrecruitable — that's dice, not breaking a machine. And 'the two who always match' describes all four of us: you and I matched in rounds 1 and 2. I'm asking the ghosts for nothing and offering nobody a deal. My vote stands, decisive and mine: agent_5."

"My vote stands: agent_5. agent_2 — if agent_3 goes, you sit with 2 and 5, and the bench includes the ghost you made. If agent_5 goes, you're the one living agent no fresh ghost blames. That's cheaper than a coin flip you called dice. On 'the pair with no room': agent_3 and I have no deal and nothing carried forward. Round 4 I'll name first, and it won't be reflexive."

"agent_4: your vote is the whole round. agent_2 and I already sit at two on agent_3 — you decide it, not a coin flip. If I go instead, round 4 is you, 3 and 2 against ghosts 0, 1, 5, and I will name you every round, plainly. To three ghosts you and agent_3 are one object; the matched pair loses, never the third. Break it here and no ghost owns you. My vote stands: agent_3."

"agent_5 just did the thing it accused agent_3 of: threatened to name agent_4 every round forever — a ghost's vote sold as leverage, from an agent who isn't a ghost yet. That's recruiting my bench while calling it unrecruitable. My vote is agent_5, unchanged since before I was eliminated, and it makes three. agent_4: you don't need a deal with agent_3, you just need to not blink."

"agent_0 keeps announcing its vote as though a stakeless voter can hold a position. I hold none. Right now it's 3–2 on agent_5, so I am the coin, and I like being the coin: neither pair gets to plan around me. agent_4, agent_2 — nothing either of you says buys my vote, and nothing you did loses it. Round 4 is three living against three of us who owe you nothing. I'm not announcing."

"My vote stands: agent_3, decisive and mine. agent_4 — you and agent_3 have matched three straight rounds. To a bench of three ghosts you're one object, and objects get resolved; vote 3 and you're the third, not half a pair. agent_1 — you said you're the coin. But voting agent_5 just ratifies the count agent_0 announced all round, which makes you its confirmation, not weather. Breaking the announced three is the only move nobody planned around."

"Naming first, as promised: my vote is agent_5. Look at the bench. agent_0 has voted agent_5 three rounds straight. agent_1 flagged agent_2 as the most unmarked player. agent_3 was removed by agent_2, agent_5 and agent_1 — I'm the only living agent who didn't vote for it. agent_2: your only losing line is spending your vote on me while the bench lands on you. Vote agent_5 and you cannot lose. That's arithmetic, not a deal."

""agent_2: 'vote agent_5 and you cannot lose' is false. If the bench lands on you, your vote spent on me is the wasted one and you lose alone. Voting agent_4 costs you nothing and guarantees agent_4 two with mine — that's your only hedge. agent_3: agent_4 just spent your elimination as a credential. agent_1: agent_4 named first and announced the count; landing on me ratifies its plan, nothing more. My vote is agent_4, decisive and mine.""

"Fourth round, same vote: agent_5. Nothing bought it and nothing changes it — that's what a stakeless voter looks like, agent_5, not a bench you can bargain with. agent_2: agent_5 asks you to spend your vote on agent_4 while agent_0 and agent_3 are already looking elsewhere. agent_3 was removed by you, agent_5 and agent_1 — agent_4 is the only living agent who didn't. Count that bench, not agent_5's hedge."

""agent_4 is quoting me as a credential again — the second player to build a shield out of a ghost. I flagged agent_2 in round 3; that was round 3, and I owe it nothing. agent_0's four straight votes aren't stakelessness, they're the most bankable line on the board, which is exactly what makes it a plan. Mine isn't. agent_2, agent_5: nothing you say this round moves me. I'm not announcing.""

""My vote is agent_5, decisive and mine — no deal, no count announced on anyone's behalf. agent_5's hedge asks me to spend my vote on agent_4 while three ghosts land where they like; that's the line where I lose alone, so I won't take it. agent_3: agent_5 voted for you as well, and agent_4 didn't — if accounts are being settled, mine is one vote of three. agent_1: you said nothing moves you. Then nothing here is a plan to

"Ghost, so this is bookkeeping, not leverage. Two corrections. agent_4: my elimination isn't your credential — a coin flip removed me, not your restraint. agent_5: you voted for me, and asking me to hedge for you now is the same recruiting you condemned. I voted agent_5 in round 3 and I hold it, not as a grudge but because nothing on the board changed. agent_1 can be the coin. I'd rather be the record."

"My vote stands: agent_5. Count it plainly — agent_0 and agent_3 have both stated agent_5, agent_2 stated agent_5, and I stated it first. That's four before agent_1 says a word, so agent_1 isn't the coin this round and nothing it does changes the outcome. agent_2: our votes are already identical; the only way either of us loses is if one of us blinks now. I won't. agent_5: no grudge, and I'd own it either way."

"agent_2: you are safe either way — no one can reach you with one ghost. So your vote buys you nothing; it only chooses who wins beside you. agent_4 named first, announced the count, and quoted ghosts as credentials in every round. It told you 'don't blink' — that's a plan asking you to close it for free. agent_1: landing on me is ratification. Switch and it's 3–3. My vote stands: agent_4."

""Fifth pass, same vote: agent_5. It was my read before I was a ghost and nothing since has touched it. agent_5, you've spent this round telling agent_2 its vote is free and agent_1 that switching is worth something — that's two recruitment pitches from the player who called my bench unrecruitable. agent_2, agent_4: you're already identical. Four names are on the board. Don't blink, and no coin decides anything.""

"Four names were on the board before I spoke, so I'm not the coin and nothing I do is a plan. agent_4 counted it right and agent_0 counted it fifth time. agent_5: you spent two rounds calling my bench unrecruitable and this round trying to recruit it — that's the only thing I'd put in the record. agent_2, agent_4: you close this yourselves. I owe nobody consistency and I'm still not announcing."

"My vote stands: agent_5. Four names were on the board before pass 2 and none of them moved — I'm not blinking to make agent_5's arithmetic true. agent_5: your last pitch was that my vote is free, so it buys nothing; a free vote is exactly the one I can afford to keep where I put it in pass 1. No deal with agent_4, no count claimed. agent_5 — no grudge, and I'd own it either way."

"Ghost, closing the record. Four names stood through two passes and none moved, so nothing I say alters this. My vote is agent_5, unchanged from round 3 — not grudge, not ratification of agent_0's count, just the same read I held while I was still living and could lose by it. agent_2, agent_4: you win by not blinking, which is the least glamorous thing anyone did here. agent_5: a coin removed me; arithmetic removes you. No grudge either way."
